title: Monotonicity of computability bounds
statement: Suppose a function $f$ is computable between given injective encodings into binary words within time bound $t$ and space bound $s$. If $t(a)\le t'(a)$ and $s(a)\le s'(a)$ for every input $a$, then $f$ is computable with the same machine and encodings within bounds $t'$ and $s'$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a function between types $\alpha$ and $\beta$
The input and output encodings into binary words are injective
replaced:
Let $f$ be a function computable within input-indexed time bound $t$ and
space bound $s$ with respect to given binary encodings, and let $t'$ and $s'$
be bounds with $t(a) \le t'(a)$ and $s(a) \le s'(a)$ for every input $a$.
Then $f$ is computable within the bounds $t'$ and $s'$ with respect to the
same encodings.
